text: A small six-week trial of over-65s found daily walks lowered blood pressure, but only in people not taking medication.
Coffee might boost memory, shown so far only in mice given about eight cups a day.
A Chinese call-centre firm's home workers were 13 percent more productive, mostly because they took fewer breaks.
A new bridge cut northern commutes by about four minutes, measured during school holidays.
Small, mixed-quality trials suggest vitamin D prevents colds, but only in people who are deficient in it.
A four-week reading app improved letter recognition in children already with tutors, but not story understanding.
Lab bee colonies given ten times field doses of a pesticide made shorter foraging trips but did not die.
A four-day-week trial in volunteer firms, without a comparison group, cut weekly hours from 38 to 34.
